---
title: "Normalized % Resistance vs Mean SF"
output: html_notebook
---

## Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## install.packages(c("ggplot2","dplyr","ggrepel","svglite"))  # run once if needed
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggrepel)
library(svglite)
```

## 1. Load & tidy data

```{r load-data}
df <- read.csv("cy5_bandquant_plot.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

names(df) <- c("replicate", "Organism", "Accession", "peak_id", "tile_id",
               "mean_sf", "perc_resistance", "norm_perc_resistance", "stall_site_rank",
               "pvalue_R1", "pvalue_R2", "pvalue_R3",
               "treated_sf_R1", "treated_sf_R2", "treated_sf_R3")

df$replicate <- factor(df$replicate)
df$Organism  <- factor(df$Organism)

head(df)
```

## 2. Correlation (across all replicate points)

```{r correlation}
ct <- cor.test(df$mean_sf, df$norm_perc_resistance, method = "pearson")
r_val <- round(unname(ct$estimate), 3)
p_val <- signif(ct$p.value, 3)
cor_label <- paste0("Pearson r = ", r_val, "\np = ", p_val)

ct
```

## 3. Per-organism summary: sf variance + resistance variance + combined p-value

`mean_sf`, the three `treated_sf_R1/R2/R3` values, and the three `pvalue_R1/R2/R3`
values are constant across the two resistance replicate rows for a given organism
(they describe the sf measurement itself, not the resistance replicate), so we pull
one copy per organism and compute:

- `sd_sf` — spread of the 3 treated-sf replicates (for horizontal error bars)
- `mean_resist` / `sd_resist` — mean & spread of the 2 resistance replicates (as before)
- `combined_p` — the 3 per-replicate p-values combined with **Fisher's method**
  (a standard way to combine independent p-values testing the same hypothesis),
  reported as `-log10(combined_p)` so higher = more significant

```{r summarize}
fisher_combine <- function(p) {
  p <- p[!is.na(p)]
  k <- length(p)
  if (k == 0) return(NA_real_)
  chi2 <- -2 * sum(log(p))
  pchisq(chi2, df = 2 * k, lower.tail = FALSE)
}

sf_p_df <- df %>%
  distinct(Organism, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    sd_sf      = sd(c(treated_sf_R1, treated_sf_R2, treated_sf_R3)),
    combined_p = fisher_combine(c(pvalue_R1, pvalue_R2, pvalue_R3)),
    neg_log10_p = -log10(combined_p)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Organism, sd_sf, combined_p, neg_log10_p)

resist_df <- df %>%
  group_by(Organism, mean_sf) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_resist = mean(norm_perc_resistance),
    sd_resist   = sd(norm_perc_resistance),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

summary_df <- resist_df %>% left_join(sf_p_df, by = "Organism")

summary_df
```

## 4. Plot

Raw replicate points are shown faded in the background; the trendline + ribbon is
fit on those raw points. The bold summary points show each organism's mean position
with **horizontal error bars = SD of the sf replicates** and **vertical error bars
= SD of the resistance replicates**, colored by **-log10(combined p-value)**
(darker/warmer = more significant).

Per-organism summary points with **horizontal error bars = SD of the sf replicates**
and **vertical error bars = SD of the resistance replicates**, colored by
**-log10(combined p-value)** (darker/warmer = more significant).

```{r plot, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.5, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
p <- ggplot() +

  # trendline + shaded standard-error ribbon (fit on all raw replicate points)
  geom_smooth(
    data = df, aes(x = mean_sf, y = norm_perc_resistance),
    method = "lm",               # swap to "loess" for a curved fit
    se = TRUE,
    color = "grey20",
    fill = "steelblue",
    alpha = 0.15,                 # faded/semi-transparent band
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +

  # raw replicate points, faded, just to show underlying spread
  geom_point(
    data = df, aes(x = mean_sf, y = norm_perc_resistance),
    color = "grey60", size = 1.6, alpha = 0.5
  ) +

  # horizontal error bars: variance in sf across the 3 treated-sf replicates
  geom_errorbarh(
    data = summary_df,
    aes(y = mean_resist, xmin = mean_sf - sd_sf, xmax = mean_sf + sd_sf),
    height = 0.02, color = "grey40"
  ) +

  # vertical error bars: variance in resistance across the 2 replicates
  geom_errorbar(
    data = summary_df,
    aes(x = mean_sf, ymin = mean_resist - sd_resist, ymax = mean_resist + sd_resist),
    width = 0.015, color = "grey40"
  ) +

  # per-organism summary point, colored by combined significance
  geom_point(
    data = summary_df,
    aes(x = mean_sf, y = mean_resist, color = neg_log10_p),
    size = 4.5
  ) +

  scale_color_viridis_c(name = expression(-log[10]("combined p-value")), option = "plasma") +

  # organism labels
  geom_text_repel(
    data = summary_df,
    aes(x = mean_sf, y = mean_resist, label = Organism),
    size = 3.2, color = "grey20", max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +

  # correlation annotation
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = min(df$mean_sf) + 0.02,
    y = max(df$norm_perc_resistance) * 0.98,
    label = cor_label,
    hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3.6, fontface = "italic"
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Mean SF",
    y = "Normalized % Resistance",
    title = "Normalized % Resistance vs Mean SF",
    subtitle = "Horiz. error = SD of 3 sf replicates; vert. error = SD of 2 resistance replicates;\ncolor = combined significance (Fisher's method); band = SE of trendline"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

p
```

## 5. Save to file

```{r save}
ggsave("resistance_vs_sf.png", p, width = 8.5, height = 6.5, dpi = 300)
ggsave("resistance_vs_sf.pdf", p, width = 8.5, height = 6.5)          # vector, for print/publication
ggsave("resistance_vs_sf.svg", p, width = 8.5, height = 6.5)          # vector, for web/editing (needs the "svglite" package)
```

Note: the SVG output requires the `svglite` package (`install.packages("svglite")`); PDF export works with base R graphics devices, no extra package needed.
